subject.title: Telegram voice message delayed ~15 minutes before agent dispatch, then run aborts

question: Should Telegram voice-message recovery add a source timestamp-to-dispatch watchdog and direct-message abort/no-response fallback, or should this issue be split into narrower polling and delivery items first?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the threshold, restart action, and direct-message fallback semantics change user-visible Telegram behavior and current tests intentionally preserve some silent no-response paths.

options.title: Define one narrow contract here
options.body: Keep this issue as canonical and specify the latency threshold, diagnostic fields, restart/alert behavior, and direct-message fallback text before implementation.

options.title: Split by subsystem
options.body: Move source-age watchdog work to a polling/ingress issue and route no-reply recovery to the existing voice delivery issue, accepting that this report remains only a cluster reference.

options.title: Limit scope to polling sleep PR
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/86541 as the only active fix path, leaving the voice-specific abort and no-reply behavior unresolved.

recommendation.title: Define one narrow contract here
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as canonical and specify the latency threshold, diagnostic fields, restart/alert behavior, and direct-message fallback text before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled ownership across Telegram polling/dispatch files and split the current polling liveness surface.
